name: ICH Score

version.label: Hemphill et al. 2001 (original)
version.detail: Five components, total 0–6. Mortality figures are the observed 30-day mortality in the derivation cohort (n = 152).

reviewStatus: Content drafted from primary sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
purpose: Standardised clinical grading of spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage severity at presentation.
intendedPopulation: Adults with spontaneous (non-traumatic) intracerebral haemorrhage, assessed at presentation.

inputs.label: ICH volume
inputs.help: Measured on initial CT, commonly by the ABC/2 method.

insights.text: Mortality figures describe a 2001 derivation cohort in which care limitations were common. Early do-not-resuscitate decisions can make prognostic scores self-fulfilling.
A high score should not by itself determine goals of care. Guidelines advise against early care limitation based on a single prognostic score.

limitations: Derived in a small single-centre cohort.
Not designed to guide individual treatment decisions.
Does not include haematoma expansion, anticoagulation, or location detail beyond supra/infratentorial.
confounders: GCS depressed by sedation, intoxication or seizures
Volume estimation error (irregular haematomas, ABC/2 overestimation)
Timing of the CT relative to symptom onset
commonErrors: Using a GCS obtained after sedation or intubation.
Measuring volume on a later scan rather than the initial CT.
Applying the score to traumatic or tumour-related haemorrhage.
doesNotTellYou: Whether surgery or any intervention is indicated.

sources.citation: Hemphill JC 3rd, Bonovich DC, Besmertis L, Manley GT, Johnston SC. The ICH score: a simple, reliable grading scale for intracerebral hemorrhage. Stroke. 2001;32(4):891-897.
Zahuranec DB, et al. Early care limitations independently predict mortality after intracerebral hemorrhage. Neurology. 2007;68(20):1651-1657.

licensing.note: No reproduction restrictions identified for the scoring criteria.

guide.what: A 0–6 grading scale combining GCS, haematoma volume, intraventricular extension, infratentorial origin and age.
guide.whenUseful: Standardised communication of ICH severity at presentation, research stratification, and as one input into prognostic discussion.
guide.howToCalculate: Use the GCS at presentation and the initial CT. Assign points for each component and sum.
guide.clinicalContext: Use as a severity descriptor, not a prognosis for an individual patient. Prognostic discussions should integrate the full clinical picture and should not rely on early scores alone.
